subject: Discovery recap: Tool calling + structured output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Tan <sara.tan@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery: Tool calling + structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Jordan & Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier - quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can make the next meeting productive. High-level pain and goals we discussed:

- Pain: Our current assistant sometimes returns free-form summaries and inconsistent fields when fetching customer data; downstream systems (billing, support ticketing) expect strict JSON payloads.
- Goal: Deterministic, schema-validated outputs for agent workflows that call internal tools (ticketing API, KB search, billing).
- Current stack: AWS-hosted microservices, an internal ticketing API, and a legacy search index. We do not have a stable schema for responses today.
- Success criteria: >95% of responses conform to the JSON schema; clear error/fallback behavior; <400ms average response time for simple data lookups.

Questions we had during the call that would help scope a POC:
1) Can Redwood's tool-calling guarantee output that adheres to an enforced JSON schema (and provide a validation failure path)?
2) How do you recommend handling partial data (fields missing from upstream APIs)?
3) What keys of the response should be considered authoritative vs optional?

Next steps from Acme: share example real payloads and our current ticketing API spec. We'd love a short POC showing tool-calling + schema enforcement on a couple of typical flows (create-ticket, fetch-customer-summary).

Attaching our internal sample responses (will send a ZIP separately). Looking forward to the demo.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Product Manager, Acme Corp
Attachments: sample-responses.zip

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: Tool calling + structured output (JSON schema)

Alex - thanks for the clear recap. Confirming what we heard and proposing a concrete plan for the POC. Summary of what Redwood will demonstrate:

- Tool calling: wire up two calls - (1) KB search -> return top answer metadata; (2) Ticketing API -> create ticket / return ticket id. Calls will be represented as functions and Redwood will surface deterministic outputs.
- Structured output: we will enforce a JSON schema at the output layer. If validation fails we will: (a) return a structured error object with validation errors, (b) include a fallback human-readable summary.
- Partial data: fields marked as optional in the schema will be omitted; required fields must either be filled or trigger the validation error path. We can also include default values where appropriate.
- Success criteria (aligned to yours): schema conformance >=95% on test prompts we co-design; end-to-end latency targets for simple lookups ~300-400ms.

I've attached an initial draft JSON schema (acme-json-schema-v0.1.json) and a short mapping doc with suggested authoritative keys. Please review and let us know if the required/optional flags line up with your downstream consumers.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share two representative input examples and the ticketing API spec (by Jul 9).
2) We run a 2-week POC that includes 1000 synthetic+real queries and a small integration to create tickets in your staging environment.
3) I'll schedule a 45-min technical demo next week to walk through the agent flow and schema enforcement.

I'll loop in Dev to scope the minimal integration work.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0123
redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery: Tool calling + structured output (JSON schema)

Adding a few implementation notes from an engineering/CS perspective:

- Agent workflow recommendation:
  1) User prompt -> natural language understanding + intent detection.
  2) If intent triggers a tool, call the tool with strongly typed args (we recommend a minimal arg schema per tool).
  3) Tool returns raw payload -> Redwood runtime applies JSON schema validation on the structured output layer.
  4) On success: emit JSON payload exactly matching the schema. On failure: emit {"status":"validation_error", "errors":[...], "fallback": "human_summary"}.

- Deterministic formatting success criteria we typically use in POCs:
  - Exact key names and types (string/number/boolean/object/array) must match schema.
  - No free-form prose in schema fields; if human text is required, it should be in a dedicated 'summary' field.
  - Include a schema-version field in the output to help downstream consumers.
  - Validation errors must be machine-parseable and include path information (e.g., data.customer.email).

- Edge-case handling:
  - Rate-limited upstream APIs: return a structured retry token and a human-friendly summary.
  - Partial upstream data: allow explicit nulls for optional fields when upstream omits values.

Dev: can you add a short example of the create-ticket function signature in a shared Drive doc? I'll include it in the demo materials.

-Marissa
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Looking forward to the demo.
